text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening thesis: \"they will not be reliable enough and will be dangerous...\"","quality":"explicit claim","description":"The essay states a direct, arguable position early so the reader immediately knows what it is trying to prove."},{"evidence":"paragraphs on danger, liability, and expense","quality":"organized reasoning","description":"The essay develops separate reasons in distinct paragraphs, which makes the argument easier to follow and more coherent."},{"evidence":"\"If it were to malfunction what could the driver do?\" and \"who is to blame?\"","quality":"rhetorical development","description":"The essay uses questions and scenarios to extend its points and make the concerns feel more concrete."},{"evidence":"\"There will need to be all new laws to avoid conflicts of who is to blame in case of an accident\"","quality":"counterargument awareness","description":"The essay acknowledges the legal problem the article raises and turns it into support for its position."},{"evidence":"concluding restatement: \"The idea of driverless cars is great but they are not reliable...\"","quality":"conclusion","description":"The essay ends by clearly summarizing its main reasons and reinforcing its overall stance."}]}
